name: Lacidipine
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Lacidipine is a dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker metabolized by the liver (CYP3A4) and excreted mainly in feces as metabolites. The Dutch label needs no kidney dose adjustment because it is not renally excreted. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: SmPC sets no kidney adjustment; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Usual: 2 mg once daily in the morning; increase to 4 mg, then 6 mg, after at least 3 to 4 weeks on each dose (SmPC).
No dose adjustment: lacidipine is not excreted by the kidneys (SmPC).

hd.text: No kidney adjustment (not renally excreted); no dialysis data in the SmPC. Highly protein-bound, so dialysis removal is unlikely.

pd.text: No kidney adjustment; no PD data.

monitoring: Blood pressure; edema; caution with conduction disease, QT prolongation and reduced cardiac reserve; avoid grapefruit (SmPC 4.4, 4.5).

renal.recommendation: Not established in children; kidney dosing not applicable.
